01·The opportunity

Seven posts in ninety days, at the highest rate in your field.

Your median engagement rate on Instagram is 3.2%. The five comparable accounts pulled over the same window run between 0.04% and 1.8% on the identical formula, and every one of them has more followers than you.

The rate is already right. The volume is not there for it to work on, and the channel with the bigger audience has been quiet since 5 July.

The strategy in one line

Instagram and LinkedIn, in English, for the builder or remodeler who already spends on marketing and cannot tell what it returns. You record once a month on one pillar. We write the scripts, cut the video, caption it, schedule both channels and report what moved.

05·Landscape·borrow and avoid

What the field rewards, and what it has worn out.

Borrow

The single case, in detail

One situation, the figures that decided it, then the decision. It travels because it is specific.

Borrow

The lane nobody publishes into: referrals for remodelers

No account in the comparable set occupies this lane, and your own commenters ask about it.

Avoid

The crowded lane: unbiased marketing advice

More than one account in the set already occupies it, so entering means competing for attention that is already spoken for.

Avoid

The repeated opener

An opener that repeats across posts teaches the audience to scroll before they read.

The clean lane

No comment questions were captured for these posts, so no lane here is backed by an audience asking. Say that plainly. What the window does support is narrower and still useful: referrals for remodelers is a subject none of the five comparables publishes into, and it is what your most recent post is about. The advisor position is the other half of it. Every account in that set sells the execution it recommends. You do not.
